findings.title: Required doorstop (or any job item) thrown behind the conveyor is lost for good, so the job can't be finished without a restart
findings.problem:
The strip of floor between the conveyor (x -0.75..7.75, z -7.45) and the kitchen back wall (z -10) can't be walked into. The west gap between the oven (x <= -1.2) and the conveyor is about 0.45 m, too narrow for Pip. At the east end, the conveyor meets the lift divider. Any prop thrown with Q while Pip faces north in the kitchen can land there.

In play I threw the doorstop from (2.8,-5.2). It came to rest at (-0.24, 0.15, -8.91). Walking toward it stalled at z -6.2 from both ends, and E there grabs a mug instead. After 10 s more it was still there: the respawn only fires above y 2.1, below y -3 or out of bounds (src/game.ts:341-342).

Without the doorstop the door can't be wedged. doorWedged() only accepts that one prop (src/lunch-runtime.ts:214). Every route into the kitchen passes through the swing door, which shuts once Pip is 2.6 m away (:224-226) and kills any cable through it (:248). The oven, fridge and conveyor feeds all run through that door. The job card keeps asking to wedge the door. The only way out is a full restart with R, which throws away all progress.

The mop, the bridges and the tray can be lost the same way. The tray is a lucky exception: within 2 m of (0,-7) it auto-places. This breaks AGENTS 7 (stuck items respawn) and AGENTS 5 (chaos never fails the job). Throwing things is the core verb, so a player will hit this.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s5-softlock.mjs and s5b-softlock.mjs logs: wedge at (-0.24,0.15,-8.91) after 10 s; walks stall at (-1.1,-7.12) and (4.3,-6.2)
findings.fix:
(1) Close the dead zone. In LunchRuntime.buildKitchen, add a solid() backsplash 0.05 m deep and 1.3 m tall along z -7.5 from x -1.2 to 7.75, and one 0.5 m filler between the oven's east side and the conveyor's west end, so props can't fall behind.
(2) Make the respawn general in src/game.ts:339-342. At level load, flood-fill a 0.5 m walkability grid from spawn against fixed colliders. Each second, any id'd dynamic item whose cell is unreachable (or y > 2.1) increments stuck. At 6 s it returns to prop.home with the dust puff.
(3) As a final safety net, a doorstop away from home and out of reach for more than 10 s while the door step is current should puff back to (-3,7).
findings.verify: New spec in tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts: 'a doorstop thrown behind the conveyor comes back'. Throw it as s5-softlock.mjs does, advance(10), then expect the wedge within 1 m of (-3,7) and grabbable. Retake lunch-play-s02 and expect an empty floor behind the belt.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the throw: from (2.83,-5.25) the doorstop came to rest at (-0.24,0.15,-8.91), walking toward it stalls at z -6.20, and 10 s later it has not moved. All of that matches. But it is not lost. The conveyor collider is only 1.1 m tall (solid 8.5×0.3×0.9 at y 0.95, src/lunch-runtime.ts:95), and Pip's jump clears about 1.36 m (vertical 7, gravity 18, src/game.ts:181,320). One Space+W from (0.02,-6.11) carried Pip over the belt to (-0.76,-9.50). There the prompt read 'E Grab the doorstop' with the marker above it, E picked it up, and Space+S jumped him back to (0.19,-3.97). It is not a soft-lock and no restart is needed. What remains is a discoverability and polish issue: the strip is out of sight, and nothing tells the player to jump the belt. A backsplash would still tidy it up.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v1-softlock.mjs log: 'wedge after throw (-0.239,0.150,-8.913)', 'after jump+W (-0.47,1.20,-8.41)', 'prompt EGrab the doorstop', 'held after E wedge', 'after jump back (0.19,0.77,-3.97)'
mockups/review5/shots/verify-lunch-play-02-jump-onto-belt.jpg (Pip behind the belt, doorstop at his feet, marker over it, prompt 'E Grab the doorstop')
findings.fix_correction: Not needed as a P0. Optionally (polish) add the 1.3 m backsplash along z -7.5 so props cannot fall behind the belt, or include the strip in the 'stranded item returns home' rule. The flood-fill respawn is overkill here, because the area is reachable by jumping.

findings.title: Pip gets pinned between the wedged right door leaf and the doorstop; movement keys stop working and only a jump frees him
findings.problem:
The wedge is dropped by the corridor (doorSide 1 at drop time), so it is fixed at (1.02, 0.2, -1.25) inside the kitchen. Coming back from the lift room along the natural path ((10,1) → (1,-0.5)), Pip stopped at (1.83,-0.60), squeezed between the open right leaf (a kinematic collider), the doorstop and the kitchen front wall.

Holding D, S, A, W, Shift+D or S+D for 1 s each did not move Pip by even 1 cm. Only Space plus S got him out. Other scripted walks to targets in every direction also stalled there for more than 60 s.

A new player has no reason to think of jumping, so in practice this is a broken control on the main route. The prompt there reads 'E Grab the doorstop', which tempts the player to un-wedge the door. That cuts every cable (see the separate finding). The camera at zoom 9 also hides Pip behind the half-wall (lunch-play-t02), so the player can't even see what is holding him.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s13-order.mjs log: STUCK at (1.82,-0.62) for every later leg
findings.fix:
(1) Seat the doorstop where nobody walks. In LunchRuntime.dropped(), place it at the leaf's free edge against the jamb on the swing side: x = 1.5 + 0.1, z = doorSide*1.42 (just past the open leaf tip), rotated to lie along the leaf.
(2) Also give the fixed wedge a smaller collider, or make it a sensor while fixed (it only has to read as 'jammed').
(3) Add a generic de-penetration in the player step (src/game.ts movement block). If input is held for more than 0.4 s and Pip moves less than 2 cm, nudge him 0.15 m along the contact normal (Rapier character controller computedCollision), or briefly allow a 0.3 m step-up.
findings.verify: Rerun s14-trap.mjs. After walking (10,1) → (1,-0.5), advance(1,['KeyD']) must move Pip more than 1 m. Add a spec 'walking from the lift room back into the kitchen past the wedged door never stalls' using route [[10,1],[1,-0.5],[-1,-2.5]].
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced exactly with the reviewer's route (v2-trap.mjs). Pip stops at (1.83,-0.57). Holding D, S, A, W, Shift+D or S+D for 1 s each leaves him at (1.83,-0.60), and only Space plus S frees him, to (3.06,-4.36). The prompt there reads 'E Grab the doorstop'. The mechanism in the finding is wrong, though. The doorstop is at (1.02,-1.25), about 1 m away on the other side of the open right leaf (the leaf lies along x≈1.4 from z 0.15 to -1.3 when doorSide is -1). Pip is east of the leaf with open floor to his east, so he is not wedged between leaf, doorstop and wall. He is pinned on the leaf's kinematic collider, probably by penetration of the 0.1 m thick cuboid. With no wedge placed (v8-leaf.mjs), the open leaf only blocks motion toward it, and S and A still move Pip, so the full pin needs the wedged-open door approached from the lift-room side. I downgraded from P0 because Jump, a button on the action bar, gets Pip out, so play is not truly blocked. Still, a dead WASD on the main route is serious.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-lunch-play-103-trapped-orbit.jpg (Pip against the leaf, doorstop on the far side of the leaf, prompt 'E Grab the doorstop')
mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v8-leaf.mjs: without a wedge the leaf only blocks motion toward it (S moves to 1.17,0.38)
src/lunch-runtime.ts:117 (leaf cuboid .72×1×.05 on a kinematic body), :227-228
findings.fix_correction: Moving the doorstop (fix 1) does not address the cause, because the doorstop is not touching Pip. Instead: (a) pass a filter to controller.computeColliderMovement (src/game.ts:321) that skips the door-leaf colliders while lunch.doorWedged() or doorAngle>0.5, or thicken the leaf cuboids to a half-depth of 0.1 and keep them as prop-only colliders. (b) Keep the generic unstuck fallback (input held >0.4 s with <2 cm of motion → nudge 0.15 m along the contact normal). Verify by rerunning s14-trap.mjs: advance(1,['KeyD']) must move Pip more than 1 m.

findings.title: The fridge spoil timer runs from second 0 with no card step, so exploring or causing chaos ends the job at 2:00
findings.problem:
LunchJob starts at temperature 0.28 and rises 0.006 per second (src/sim/lunch.ts:8). The job fails at exactly t = 120 s unless the fridge is fed or the cooler box (locked in the dark storeroom) is used. Idling, I saw:
- the HUD bar turn warm at about 45 s;
- the sad-food icon over the fridge at about 87 s (lunch-play-f01 at 0.79, f02 at 1:57);
- the job end with the spoil card at 2:00 (f04).

The job card's 7 steps never mention the fridge (src/ui/objectives.ts:40-50). It only appears as the third bonus, whose wording is on the pause and result screens. For the whole first two minutes the card says 'Wedge…', 'Mop…', 'Power the feed post…'.

The scripted bot only survives because the spec plugs the fridge at 31 s, as step 3 of its own plan. A new player who walks the card's steps in order, plays with the bots, throws things at the crowd or simply reads the room will spoil the lunch long before reaching the capacitor puzzle. The penalty is the harshest in the game: a full restart of a 7-step chain.

This is a timer fail, not a mistake in the taught concept made by the player's own decision. It punishes the Good Job-style messing about that AGENTS 5 protects, and the hidden fridge requirement is a hidden rule (DR-37).
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s6-fail.mjs log: t85 temp 0.79, failed at t=120.0
findings.fix:
Pick one, ideally (a) together with (b).
(a) Add a first card step 'Keep the lunch in the fridge cold' (done when the fridge has been powered for 2 s, or when cooled), with the marker on the fridge socket (-4,-1.8). Turn on the fridge socket ring pulse from the start.
(b) Soften the fail. Spoiling no longer ends the job: the fridge groans, the sad icon stays, cost +60, and the third bonus is lost. The tray can still be delivered, so the only job-ending fail is the burned tray, which comes from a sequencing decision.
(c) If the hard fail stays: start at 0.0 and use a rate of 0.0035 (about 285 s). Also hold the warming until Pip first opens the kitchen door, so exploration time isn't counted.
findings.verify: Spec: open the level, advance(150) without touching anything. Expect job.failed false (option b or c), or expect the card's current step to name the fridge at t = 0 (option a). Retake lunch-play-f02 and check that the card text and the marker point at the fridge.
findings.verify_reason: The arithmetic holds: 0.28 + 0.006/s reaches 1.0 at 120 s (src/sim/lunch.ts:5,8). Idling reproduced it: at t 119.9 the temperature was 0.999 and failed was false, and at t 120.0 failed was true and the spoil card dropped. None of the card's steps mention the fridge (src/ui/objectives.ts:40-50), and in the reviewer's f02 the card still says 'Wedge…' at 1:57 while the bar is red. One qualification: this is not entirely a hidden rule. The HUD fridge thermometer is visible from t=0, and the sad icon appears at 0.8. The spoil fail is also an explicit design decision (docs/LEVEL_02_LUNCH_RUSH.md:14 'at red the food spoils (job fails, retry). Already warming at start.'). So AGENTS 5, which covers destruction, does not strictly apply. The real problem is a 2-minute fuse on a 7-step chain with no card step pointing at it.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v7-retry.mjs log: 't 119.9 failed? false temp 0.999', 't 120.0 failed true'
mockups/review5/shots/lunch-play-f02-fridge-sad-118s.jpg (card still on step 1 at 1:57, HUD bar red)
findings.fix_correction: Option (b), making spoiling not end the job, contradicts the product doc (LEVEL_02:14), so it needs owner sign-off. Prefer (a), a fridge card step or a marker pulse from t=0, together with (c), a slower rate or a warming hold until the kitchen door first opens.

findings.title: The R keycap on the Retry and Play-again buttons does nothing, while R during play reloads the job instantly with no confirmation
findings.problem:
The fail card's Retry button and the result card's replay button both show an 'R' keycap (src/ui/screens.ts:198, :225). Pressing R on the fail card did nothing: no navigation within 5 s, or within 60 s in a second run.

The cause is in the key handlers. GameUI.key only sets the autostart flag for KeyR (src/ui/game-ui.ts:119). The game's own KeyR handler requires playing = running && !won (src/game.ts:166), and both fail and win set won = true. Clicking Retry or pressing Enter works and is fast (0.7 s to play), so the retry itself is cheap, but the key the button shows is dead. This looks like a side effect of the L6 fix ('Tab and R only act during play').

The reverse is worse. During play, R calls location.reload() at once (src/game.ts:178). R sits next to E on the keyboard, and Lunch is the longest chain in the game (92 s for the bot, several minutes for a person). One stray press wipes everything, with no hold or confirm.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s8-retry.mjs log: 'R navigated? false', 'click retry -> ready ms 685'
mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s7-burn.mjs: waitForNavigation timeout after KeyR on the burn card
findings.fix:
(1) In GameUI.key, add: if (e.code==='KeyR' && (s==='fail'||s==='result')) { e.preventDefault(); this.restart(); }
(2) During play, make R a hold. Keep a 0.8 s hold timer with a ring filling on a small 'Hold R to restart' chip, and only call action('restart') when it completes. Or route a single R press to the pause menu's Restart button with focus on it.
findings.verify: Extend s8-retry.mjs: on the fail card, pressing R must navigate within 2 s. During play, a single R press must not navigate, and holding R for 1 s must. Add both checks to tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. On the spoil card, KeyR did nothing for 4 s (no main-frame navigation, screen stayed 'fail'), while Enter navigated at once. In code, GameUI.key only sets flagAutostart for KeyR (src/ui/game-ui.ts:119). The game's KeyR handler requires playing = running && !won (src/game.ts:166), and failing sets won = true (src/lunch-runtime.ts:285). The R keycap is drawn on both buttons (src/ui/screens.ts:198,225, visible in my fail-card shot). During play, R calls location.reload() immediately with no hold or confirm (src/game.ts:178), and R sits next to E.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v7-retry.mjs log: 'R on fail card navigated? false screen fail', 'Enter navigated? true'

findings.title: The cable slingshot is unreachable in Lunch and there is nothing to fling
findings.problem:
I dragged thin-2 (30 m, from cart A at (-13,3)) east along the corridor at a sprint, then kept holding sprint into the east wall. Strain only reached 0.99 at x = 16, the room's edge. The Q slingshot prompt appears at 0.97, so it shows for a moment.

Releasing with Q moved no id'd item more than 0.3 m and alarmed nobody. The fastest prop was 5e-6 m/s, damage 0 and no shake. The reason: the reels are 30-32 m and the room is 33 m wide. release() needs energy > 1 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:200), and that needs strain well above 1, which the walls make impossible. Rope only wraps around level.obstacles, so a player would have to deliberately route a loop around the dividers to stretch it.

The thick cable is heavier but has the same 30 m. There is also no fling target like the Playground pins. The strain colour itself reads well (orange and red in lunch-play-x03), so the build-up is there with no payoff. AGENTS 4 names the slingshot as the cable's signature act, and DR-06 requires a reward in reach.
findings.fix:
(1) Turn thin-3, the spare loose cable at (-11,7) that the solution never needs, into a short 14 m 'slingshot' lead plugged into cart B's free socket: addCable('thin-3',3,14,'b',null,[-9,7]).
(2) In the corridor 15-18 m east of cart B, within reel length plus a sprint, add a fling target: a stacked tower of 10 cups and trays on the lunch-crowd bench at (3,9), or a tray-pyramid like the pins. Give it a bonus 'Topple the cup tower' in JOBS.lunch.bonuses with a confetti burst.
(3) Lower the release threshold to energy > 0.4, and scale the impulse by strain beyond 0.9 so a 0.99 release still gives a small fling.
findings.verify: New spec: take thin-3, sprint toward (6,9) with advance(2,['KeyD','ShiftLeft']), press Q. Expect snapshot().alarmed >= 1 and the cup-tower bonus true. Retake lunch-play-x04 and expect cups in flight.
findings.verify_reason: The slingshot is reachable. I took thin-2 at spawn and walked the route a lift or conveyor feed actually takes: corridor → kitchen door → (3,-2.6) → (7.3,-1.2) → the gap at (9.2,-1) → (14,-6) → the lift-room corner. Strain climbed to 1.028, about 0.84 m past length, so energy ≈ 42 > 1 (src/sim/cable.ts:71). The pull caps it, as designed. On Q, fastestProp was 8.22 m/s and damage went 0→2, so clutter along the cable was flung and broke. The reviewer's test only stretched the cable straight along the corridor, where 30 m does not reach the east wall from cart A. Two points stand: no NPC was alarmed in that corner (alarmed 0), and there is no dedicated fling target like the Playground pins. That is polish.
findings.fix_correction: Keep only the optional parts: a fling target or bonus (a cup tower) placed where a routed cable ends naturally (the lift room or kitchen), and/or a short spare lead. Lowering the energy threshold is unnecessary.

findings.title: The win push-in frames the underside of the lift car and leaves Pip out of the shot
findings.problem:
On delivery the camera pushes in on winFocus (12, 2.2, -7), offset 2.2 m right, at distance 9 and pitch 0.6 (src/game.ts:373-374, :398). By then the lift car has risen to y about 3.6. The frame (lunch-play-c20, c21) is filled by the grey underside of the car, a tiny tray, confetti and the capacitor cart at the bottom edge. Pip, who did the work and is standing at the winch at (11.8,-4.4), is not in frame at all.

The result tag then covers the right half. This is the payoff moment for the longest job in the game, and it reads as a camera glitch. QA 10 and R2 P0.1 asked for Pip in the win shot, and this still fails for Lunch.
findings.fix: In winFocus(), for lunch return the midpoint of Pip's position and the lift car top: new T.Vector3((p.x+12)/2, 1.8, (p.z-7)/2). In the push-in for lunch use distance 11, pitch 0.42, and offset left by 1.5 m rather than right 2.2 m, so the tag on the right doesn't cover the subject. Optionally play a cheer pose on Pip, facing the lift.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-play-c20 after the clean route (s2-clean.mjs). Pip's bounding box and the lift car must both sit within the centre 70% of the frame, left of the result tag.
findings.verify_reason: My own clean run (v3-clean.mjs, won at 91.8 s) gives the same frame. The camera pushes in close on the lift car with confetti and the capacitor cart at the bottom, and only a cropped sliver of Pip's hat shows in the bottom-left corner. The result tag covers the right half. Correction: what fills the frame is the car's raised deck and back wall seen from above, with the small tray on it, not its underside. The code matches: winFocus is (12,2.2,-7) + right*2.2, at distance 9 and pitch 0.6 (src/game.ts:373,398).

findings.title: The first prompt contradicts the card and leads a new player straight into a door-cut
findings.problem:
Pip spawns at (-10,5), 1.5 m from thin-2's loose end at (-10,3.5) (src/levels/lunch.ts:37, src/lunch-runtime.ts:61). The first frame (lunch-play-01) shows the card 'Wedge the kitchen door open with the doorstop' and the prompt 'F Pick up the thin cable end'. Those are the only two lines of text, and they point at different objects.

I followed the prompt like a new player: F, then walk to the kitchen post. The unwedged door shut behind Pip while he was still carrying the cable, and the cable was already DEAD before reaching the post. There was a red badge at the door (lunch-play-n02), and the prompt then said 'Repair the burned cable (costs 15)'.

So the game's own advice causes the first failure within 4 seconds. The marker does point at the doorstop. But the prompt pill sits just above the action bar, right where the player looks, and it wins.
findings.fix:
(1) Move thin-2's loose end away from spawn: addCable('thin-2',3,30,'a',null,[-12,2.4]). Or move spawn to (-7.5,6.2), between the dolly and the doorstop, facing the corridor.
(2) In promptFor for lunch, while the current step is the door or the mop, suppress the 'Pick up the … cable end' prompt unless the player has already done step 1. Instead, show the step item's prompt when it is within 1.75 m, and nothing otherwise. That keeps the prompt and the marker on the same object.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-play-01-start. The prompt must be empty or name the doorstop. Add a unit check in tests: at t = 0 on lunch, promptFor() is null or contains 'doorstop'.
findings.verify_reason: At t=0 the card reads 'Wedge the kitchen door open with the doorstop' while the prompt reads 'F Pick up the thin cable end' (v3-clean and v4 logs). Following the prompt into the kitchen with the door unwedged gets the cable cut by the door. In my slingshot run thin-2 went black and the prompt became 'F Repair the burned cable (costs 15)'. Spawn (-10,5) is 1.5 m from thin-2's loose end (-10,3.5) (src/levels/lunch.ts:27, src/lunch-runtime.ts:61), and the Lunch prompt takes precedence (src/ui/objectives.ts:68).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v3-clean.mjs log row 'start': card 'Wedge…', prompt 'F Pick up the thin cable end'

findings.title: 'E Grab the doorstop' near the wedged door is a trap: one press un-wedges the door and cuts every cable through it
findings.problem:
Once the door is wedged, Pip passes it on almost every later leg. nearest() favours any id'd item by 2 m (src/game.ts:192-194), so whenever Pip is within 1.65 m of the jammed doorstop the prompt reads 'E Grab the doorstop' (lunch-play-t02, t03; s13 log, repeatedly). E is the verb the player presses most, for bridges, the tray, the shelf and the cart.

Picking the doorstop up makes it dynamic again (src/game.ts:228). The door then auto-closes and kills every cable through it (src/lunch-runtime.ts:248): the thick kitchen feed, the fridge feed and the conveyor feed. Each costs 15 to repair, the oven stops, and the bake regresses. The prompt gives no hint of this, so the forgiving-interaction rule turns into an unfair, invisible fail.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s13-order.mjs log: prompt 'E Grab the doorstop' at multiple steps
findings.fix:
(1) In Game.nearest(), skip the doorstop while lunch.doorWedged() is true and any cable crosses the door rectangle. Lunch can expose a doorBusy() helper that reuses the segmentHits test from :248. Lunch then shows no prompt there.
(2) If un-wedging must stay possible, require F-hold or a second press within 1 s, and show the prompt text 'Unwedge the door (it will shut on your cables)'.
findings.verify: Spec: after the clean route's kitchen feed, walk to (1.3,-0.9) and press E. Expect held !== 'wedge', doorWedged true, and thick not dead. Retake t03: the prompt must not offer the doorstop.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. With the kitchen fed by the thick cable and the door wedged, the prompt near the door read 'E Grab the doorstop'. E picked it up (held wedge, doorWedged false). After walking to (-3,-4.5), the door shut and thick became 'b,kitchen:DEAD', the oven went off, and the card regressed to 'Keep the oven on until the tray is baked'. In code, ids get a 2 m bias in reach() (src/game.ts:192-194), the doorstop turns dynamic again on grab (:226), and the door cut is at src/lunch-runtime.ts:248.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v4-interact.mjs log: 'F7 near wedge … prompt E Grab the doorstop', 'F7 after E held wedge wedged false', 'thick:b,kitchen:DEAD oven off'

findings.title: Pressing E at a supply cart that isn't tripped silently unplugs a cable, so a double tap on reset kills the fridge feed
findings.problem:
In LunchRuntime.interact(), E (cableOnly false) first tries a breaker reset on a tripped cart. If no cart is tripped, it falls through to the switches and then to 'nearby cable ends within 1.75 m', which it unplugs and puts in Pip's hand (src/lunch-runtime.ts:162-169).

At cart A, with nothing tripped, E picked up thin-1 straight out of the cart (s3 log 'after reset: lheld thin-1'). In another run E at the cart produced 'stop:fridge': the fridge feed was pulled and the fridge began warming again.

The classic way to hit this is to press E to reset a trip, then press E again because nothing obvious happened. The second press unplugs a working feed. The prompt gives no warning, because once the breaker is reset the reset prompt is gone and E silently becomes 'unplug'. F is the cable key elsewhere (DR-22), but in Lunch both E and F grab cable ends.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s3-newbie.mjs log: 'at cart A … prompt F Pick up the thin cable end' then after E: 'lheld thin-1', thin-1 ports ','
findings.fix: In interact(), when !cableOnly, return false before the 'nearby cable' branch. E should never grab cable ends in Lunch, so only F plugs and unplugs, matching DR-22. Also add a 0.5 s lockout after resetBreaker() during which E at that cart does nothing.
findings.verify: Spec: plug thin-1 into the fridge, walk to (-12,4), press E twice. Expect thin-1 ports to still include 'a' and 'fridge', and fridge state 'on'.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. At (-11.74,4.13) beside the untripped cart A, E (not F) pulled thin-1 out of the cart: lheld thin-1, ports 'a' cleared. After F put it back, a second E pulled it out again. The code path is src/lunch-runtime.ts:160-169: with no trip and no switch nearby, E falls through to the 'nearby cable' branch. Two qualifications lower the priority. The prompt there does say 'F Pick up the thin cable end', and after the unplug the end is visibly in Pip's hand with an F plug prompt. So it is not silent, and one press undoes it.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v5-cart.mjs log: 'pip -11.74 4.13 … prompt F Pick up the thin cable end', 'after E lheld thin-1 thin-1:,', 'after E2 thin-1'

findings.title: The thick-cable dolly parks in the kitchen doorway and blocks the only route between corridor and kitchen
findings.problem:
While the thick cable is held, the dolly is velocity-driven straight toward Pip whenever it is more than 1.3 m away (src/lunch-runtime.ts:237). It ignores the cable path, so it trails right behind Pip through the doorway. After the plug-in it is a free dynamic prop, and Pip shoves it while walking back out.

In three separate runs it ended at about (0.36,-1.2), in the door opening beside the wedge (lunch-play-d04). Walking out stalled at (-0.48,-1.30) in the clean run and in s9, and in s9 the stall made a later leg (to the fridge) fail entirely.

The player has to find 'E Grab the cable dolly (heavy: push it)' and shove it aside, and it sits in the most-used 3 m opening in the level. DR-74 also asks for a follow distance of at least 2 m along the cable path. This is still 1.3 m and a straight line.
findings.fix:
(1) Follow along the rope: target the cable point 2.2 m back from Pip along cable.points, rather than Pip himself, and only while d > 2.2.
(2) When the thick end is plugged or dropped and the dolly is within 2.2 m of DOOR, glide it over 0.5 s to the nearest parking spot outside the opening: (-2.6,-1.0) inside or (-2.6,1.2) outside.
(3) Raise the dolly's mass and linear damping so a walking Pip doesn't shove it, and make it 'grab to push' only.
findings.verify: Rerun s10-dolly.mjs. After plugging the post, walk(.3,-1.3) must arrive, and the dolly must be more than 1.8 m from (0,0). Retake d04 and expect a clear doorway.
findings.verify_reason: The reviewer's d04 shows the dolly parked in the door opening beside the doorstop, with Pip next to it. My clean run also stalled walking back out: 'STUCK 0.3 -1.3 at (-0.48,-1.39)'. In code, the dolly is driven straight at Pip whenever it is more than 1.3 m away, ignoring the cable path (src/lunch-runtime.ts:237). That contradicts DR-74 (≥2 m along the cable path).
findings.fix_correction: Some doorway stalls may come from the door-leaf collider (finding 1) rather than the dolly. Verify both with the s10 route after fixing.

findings.title: On a phone the Lunch chain HUD covers the job card, and the survey shows only the kitchen middle
findings.problem:
At 390×844:
- The Lunch-only chain strip (oven → belt → lift + fridge bar) is drawn across the top of the job card, hiding its progress dots (lunch-play-06).
- The breaker-gauge panel sits on top of the prompt pill's row and next to the camera button.
- The survey (Tab, fixed zoom 44, src/game.ts:366) frames only the kitchen and the doorway (lunch-play-07). The power room with both carts, the storeroom, the lift room, the lunch crowd and Pip himself are all off screen.

The survey is a phone player's main tool for planning a seven-step route, and it fails here. DR-21 requires every wall and the goal visible in portrait. The desktop survey (lunch-play-02) is fine.
findings.fix:
(1) CSS for body[data-touch] .lunch-chain (or @media (max-aspect-ratio:1/1)): place it under the card (top: card bottom + 8 px), or shrink it to a single row inside the timer pill.
(2) In updateCamera, pick the survey zoom by aspect: zoom = 44 * clamp((level.width/level.depth)/(cam.aspect*1.6), 1, 2.4). Or, for portrait, turn yaw 90° so the 33 m axis runs vertically.
(3) Move the phone breaker panel to the right edge above the action buttons.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-play-06 and -07 at 390×844. The card dots must be visible. The survey must show cart A/B, the storeroom, the lift and Pip. Run this for every cable floor.
findings.verify_reason: Looked at both 390×844 shots. The lunch chain strip sits over the top of the job card and hides its progress dots. The breaker panel shares the prompt pill's row. The Tab survey shows only the kitchen and the doorway, with no carts, storeroom, lift room or Pip. The survey uses a fixed zoom of 44 and a fixed room centre whatever the aspect ratio (src/game.ts:366-368), and cam.aspect<1 only changes follow.

findings.title: The fridge, the pendant lamps and the kitchen half-wall hide Pip at close zoom, because only pillars fade
findings.problem:
At zoom 9 by the storeroom door, the 2.3 m fridge fills the middle of the screen and Pip is completely hidden behind it (lunch-play-v04). A low orbit there puts a pendant lamp shade over Pip's head and face (v05). At the wedged door, Pip shows only his hat above the kitchen front half-wall (t02), at exactly the moment he is stuck and the player needs to see why.

The occlusion fade only covers meshes in game.occluders (pillars), and it casts one ray to Pip's chest (src/game.ts:387-388). None of the Lunch kitchen machines built in buildKitchen (fridge, oven hood, shelf) are registered, and neither are the decor pendants or the front walls.
findings.fix:
(1) In buildKitchen and buildLift, push the meshes of the fridge body, the oven and hood, the lift posts and the winch housing into game.occluders, and do the same for the kitchen front wall and the dividers, with their materials set transparent-capable.
(2) In updateCamera, cast three rays (feet p.y-0.6, chest p.y+0.4, head p.y+1.0) and fade to 0.2.
(3) Hide pendant shades when their bounding box falls between the camera and Pip's head.
findings.verify: Retake v04, v05 and t02. At least 70% of Pip's pixels must be visible, and the faded fridge and wall at no more than 25% opacity.
findings.verify_reason: In v04 at zoom 9, the fridge fills the screen centre and Pip is hidden. In v05 a pendant shade covers Pip's head. In code, only meshes pushed to game.occluders fade (src/game.ts:113,387-388), and buildKitchen and buildLift add none (src/lunch-runtime.ts:73-106).
findings.fix_correction: When registering the kitchen machines as occluders, clone their materials first. toon()/glossyToon materials may be shared, and the fade writes material.opacity and depthWrite per material (src/game.ts:388), so fading a shared one would fade other meshes too.

findings.title: Clutter crates in job yellow sit next to the yellow doorstop and read as job items
findings.problem:
The Lunch clutter palette includes '#ffc94d' (src/levels/lunch.ts:19), the exact yellow used for job items: the doorstop, the feed post, cart A, the bridges and the thick cable. The start and survey shots show at least 6 bright yellow crates around the corridor, the lift room and the vending area (lunch-play-01 at about (960,590), lunch-play-02, c01, c02, x01).

The first task is 'find the doorstop', a small ridged yellow wedge on the floor, so the yellow crates are direct false affordances. In c01 the yellow crate beside the mop looks just as much like 'the thing to grab' as the doorstop did. The job-yellow language (ART R1.2) only works if nothing decorative uses it.
findings.fix: In src/levels/lunch.ts clutter.colors, replace '#ffc94d' with a kraft or neutral tone, for example ['#c98f5a','#d7a56d','#5f8fa8','#b9a27a','#e9f0f2']. Add a unit test over every level's clutter.colors that rejects any colour within ΔE 25 of #ffc94d, #ffc629 or #ffd84a.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-play-01 and -02 and count the yellow non-job props (expect 0). Add a unit test in tests/ for the palette.
findings.verify_reason: The clutter palette includes '#ffc94d' (src/levels/lunch.ts:18, not :19). Bright yellow tape-crates appear in my c14 (right of the lift), my sling shot (lift-room corner) and the reviewer's f02 (bottom). It is a real false-affordance risk for job yellow. I downgraded because the crates are box-shaped with tape, while the job doorstop is a ridged wedge with a marker over it and a prompt.

findings.title: Lunch's grade can't fail: the default 120 s limit plus best-of-three means every run earns an A
findings.problem:
Lunch passes no limits, so grade() uses 120 s, 10 damage and 300 cost (src/game.ts:354, src/sim/grade.ts:3).

The scripted clean run took 91.8 s of simulated time (it sprints everywhere, never hesitates, and overlaps the bake) and graded A/A/A. A person will take several minutes, so the time axis will usually read B to D. Damage stays far under 10 for anyone not wrecking deliberately, and the overall grade is the best axis, so effectively every completed Lunch is an A. Meanwhile a player who wrecks a lot still gets an A on time if fast.

The result card also highlights the time row as the grade source (c21), even though all three axes are equal. The grade gives no signal about understanding (tripping breakers or scorching cables don't count as damage at all, only as lost bonus stars).
findings.fix:
(1) Add optional limits to Level, and pass this.station?.limits ?? this.level.limits into grade(). For lunch use {time:300, damage:4, cost:60}.
(2) Count each breaker trip, short or scorch as +1 damage and +10 cost (the circuit event log already exists), so mistakes in the taught concept move a grade axis.
(3) On the result card, mark which axis gave the overall grade.
findings.verify: Unit test grade() with the lunch limits: a 92 s / 0 / 15 run gives A, and a 400 s / 6 / 90 run gives B or lower overall. Rerun s2-clean.mjs: the result shows A.
findings.verify_reason: Lunch passes no limits, so it uses the default 120/10/300 (src/game.ts:354, src/sim/grade.ts:3). The clean run (91.8 s, 2 damage, 15 cost) gave A/A/A. That contradicts DR-07 (axes tuned per room). However, 'every completed run earns an A' follows from AGENTS hard rule 6 (overall = best of three). Per-room limits will not change that for any tidy player. They only make the axis medals meaningful.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v3-clean.mjs: 'won true time 91.78', result A/A/A/A, dmg 2, cost 15
findings.fix_correction: Keep best-of-three (AGENTS 6). Add Level.limits for lunch (e.g. time 300) so the time medal reflects the longer chain, and optionally count trips and scorches in cost. Do not frame it as making the overall grade fail.

findings.title: A clean, careful run already shows '2 broken': placing the tray and pushing the capacitor cart count as damage
findings.problem:
In the scripted clean run, damage went from 0 to 1 (cost +10) the moment the tray went onto the conveyor, and to 2 (cost +15) while pushing the capacitor cart to the winch. Both were logged at those steps.

The tray becomes kinematic and is teleported to (-0.5,1.18,-7) with setNextKinematicTranslation (src/lunch-runtime.ts:277-278). Rapier reports a large apparent velocity, and the next frame's speed drop trips the impact check (lastSpeed > 5.5 and drop > 3.5, src/game.ts:337), which marks the tray itself as broken. The pushed cart, driven by setLinvel ×12, bumps clutter at speed.

From the second step on, the HUD tally reads '1 broken' and then '2'. That tells a tidy player they broke something, which undermines the damage axis as feedback.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s2-clean.mjs log: 'tray on belt … dmg 1 cost 10', 'at winch … dmg 2 cost 15'
findings.fix:
(1) In the damage loop, skip props with spec.id, or with kinematic or fixed bodies.
(2) When placing the tray, call body.setTranslation (not setNext…) and set prop.lastSpeed = 0, damaged = true.
(3) Cap the pushed heavy prop's impulse transfer by setting damaged = true for clutter hit by a held heavy job item at under 6 m/s.
findings.verify: Rerun s2-clean.mjs. Expect damage 0 at 'tray on belt' and at 'cap docked'.
findings.verify_reason: In my clean run, damage went 0→1 (cost 10) on 'tray on belt' and 1→2 (cost 15) at 'at winch' during the capacitor-cart push. The HUD tally reads 2 in c14. The root cause (a kinematic teleport tripping the impact check, src/lunch-runtime.ts:277-278, src/game.ts:335) is plausible, but I did not isolate which prop was marked damaged.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v3-clean.mjs log: 'tray on belt … dmg 1 cost 10', 'at winch … dmg 2 cost 15'

findings.title: The card skips the conveyor, so the HUD chain says 'conveyor' while the card says 'lift' and the start order is never shown
findings.problem:
After the tray is placed, the card jumps to 'Start the lift winch without tripping a breaker' (src/ui/objectives.ts:49). Its marker points at the winch. At the same time, the top HUD chain highlights the conveyor icon as the current stage (lunch-play-c11 to c17).

The conveyor needs its own cable and switch (thin-2 → (5,-5), E). Its start-up kick is also why the design wants 'conveyor before lift' (LEVEL_02 step 6). Neither appears on the card or in the world, so the two only UI elements disagree about what comes next.

The 'Send the tray up' step's marker does fall back to the conveyor (:50), but only after the lift has run.
findings.fix: Insert a card step after 'Carry the tray': {text:'Get the conveyor moving', done:g=>g.lunch.powered('conveyor')||job.transport>0, at:()=>({x:5,z:-5})}. Then 'Start the lift winch…' and 'Send the tray up'. This also makes the dots match the 3-stage HUD chain.
findings.verify: Retake c14: the card and the HUD chain both point at the conveyor, and the marker sits over the blue motor box.
findings.verify_reason: In c14 the card says 'Start the lift winch without tripping a breaker' with the marker on the winch, while the HUD chain highlights the conveyor stage. The conveyor has no card step (src/ui/objectives.ts:46-50).

findings.title: A door-cut cable is called 'burned', and repairing it while it still runs through the shut door just cuts it again
findings.problem:
After the swing door cut thin-2 (n02), the prompt read 'F Repair the burned cable (costs 15)' (src/lunch-runtime.ts:195). Nothing burned: the cause was the door, and the in-world badge is a lightning bolt.

The repair branch (:169) only clears lead.dead and charges 15. The cable still passes through the unwedged door, so it is cut again as soon as Pip walks off. A new player can pay 15 twice and learn the wrong lesson ('cables burn out'). The two failure causes (heat scorch versus mechanical cut) teach different things and should be named differently.
findings.fix: Store lead.cause = 'cut'|'scorch' where dead is set (:248 sets 'cut'; scorch is in the circuit). The prompt becomes 'Splice the cut cable (15)' or 'Replace the scorched cable (15)'. While the door is unwedged and the cable crosses it, show 'Wedge the door first' and refuse the splice.
findings.verify: Rerun s3-newbie.mjs: the prompt says 'cut', and pressing F there with the door unwedged doesn't charge cost.
findings.verify_reason: Seen in play: a door-cut thin-2 gives the prompt 'F Repair the burned cable (costs 15)'. src/lunch-runtime.ts:195 uses one label for any dead lead. Nuance: after a repair the cable is not cut again 'as soon as Pip walks off'. The cut fires only on the door's open→shut transition (:226,248), so it happens on the next pass through the unwedged door.

findings.title: The burn warning is nearly invisible: only a slightly redder oven window and a beep
findings.problem:
After baking, the tray waits on the oven door. From 60 s (BURN_WARNING) the oven window swaps to HOT_WINDOW and a beep sounds every 2 s (src/lunch-runtime.ts:280-282, :294). At the game camera (lunch-play-b02, 1:43, ovenWait 64 s), the oven looks almost the same as during a normal bake: no smoke visible, no badge, and the tray is a tiny item that is hard to see (b01).

The burn then ends the job with a card (b04). The fridge gets a sad-food badge before it spoils, but the burn has no matching cue. DR-47 says device state should show on the device.
findings.fix:
(1) From BURN_WARNING, float a pulsing warning sprite (reuse warningTexture or a 'burnt tray' glyph) over the oven at y 2.6, and emit smoke puffs at twice the current rate from the oven top.
(2) Flash the HUD chain's oven icon red.
(3) Raise the baked tray's spawn to the oven top (y 1.75) with a bright cloche, so it reads at the game camera.
findings.verify: Retake lunch-play-b02 at ovenWait 65 s. A first-time viewer can tell 'the oven is about to burn something' without the HUD.
findings.verify_reason: In b02 (1:43, past BURN_WARNING), the oven window looks like a normal bake glow, there is no badge, and the tray is a tiny item beside Pip. The only cues are HOT_WINDOW, a smoke puff at rate 3 and a beep every 2 s (src/lunch-runtime.ts:280-282,294).

findings.title: An unplugged spare cable is tethered to a fixed point in empty floor
findings.problem:
thin-3 starts loose at both ends near cart B (src/lunch-runtime.ts:61). Picking up one end and walking away builds strain against its other end, which stays nailed at (-11.5,0.18,7): strain 0.21, 0.36, 0.55, 0.74 and then 0.81 at about 26 m (s4 log, lunch-play-x01).

A loose cable should come along with you, not act as if plugged into the floor. This makes cable behaviour inconsistent ('which end is anchored?') and wastes the third cable as a toy.
findings.fix: In step(), when the non-held end has no port (cable.ports[other] === null) and strain > 0.75, drag that end along the rope toward Pip so strain is capped at 0.75 (ends[other].lerp(points[1], …)), with a scraping sound and dust. Or make thin-3 the short 14 m slingshot lead plugged into B, as in the slingshot finding.
findings.verify: Rerun s4-chaos.mjs. The loose drag strain stays at or below 0.8 and ends[0] moves.
findings.verify_reason: Checked in code. thin-3 is created with both ports null (src/lunch-runtime.ts:61). When one end is held, the other end becomes rope.anchor (:241-243) and nothing ever moves it, so strain builds against a fixed point on the floor. I did not rerun the drag myself; the strain numbers come from the reviewer's s4 log.

findings.title: The close of the job is mostly waiting: a long cart push, then 9 s of belt and 6 s of lift with nothing to do
findings.problem:
The longest single leg in the clean route is pushing the heavy capacitor cart from the storeroom to the winch: 11.5 s of simulated sprint, with a slower walk for a person, passing nothing to interact with. DR-09 allows 8 s.

After the last action the player watches transport for 9 s (src/sim/lunch.ts:14, dt/9) and then lift for 6 s (:15, dt/6). In the clean run the lift step and the 'Done' were about 6 s apart, and up to 15 s if the conveyor was started last. That is fine as a short payoff, but at 15 s with nothing to do or react to, it is dead time.
findings.fix:
(1) Belt transport to 5 s and lift to 4 s.
(2) Add a 'ride along' moment: the lunch crowd turns, cheers and walks toward the lift as the tray rises. The camera starts the win push-in as the lift starts, not at delivery.
(3) Move the capacitor cart's start to (-9.5,-5.5), nearer the storeroom door, or give it a 'roll' boost (push speed 1.2×), so the leg stays under 8 s.
findings.verify: Rerun s2-clean.mjs: the 'at winch' leg is under 8 s and lift-on to won is under 5 s.
findings.verify_reason: In my clean run the capacitor-cart push leg took 11.5 s ('at winch dt 11.5'). From lift-on (85.6) to the win (91.8) there was 6.2 s of locked waiting. DR-09 allows 8 s for a walk and 3 s for a locked wait. The rates are dt/9 and dt/6 (src/sim/lunch.ts:13-14).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v3-clean.mjs log: 'at winch dt 11.5', 'lift on t 85.6' → 'end t 91.8'

findings.title: The dark storeroom is still a tinted lid plane; boxes and the lamp show through it while only the cart is hidden
findings.problem:
The storeroom darkness is still an unlit plane at y 1.5 with opacity 0.8 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:64-66). From the game camera the room's crates, bins and floor lamp are all clearly visible, just purple-tinted, and the lamp shade at 2.2 m is drawn untinted above the lid (lunch-play-v01, 01-start, 03).

Meanwhile the capacitor cart and cooler box are made invisible, and props inside can't be grabbed (:143-145, :293). So the room doesn't read as 'pitch dark, find a light'. It reads as 'a purple room with some boxes and nothing useful'. The player gets no cue that something important is hidden there. LR1, raised in R1, R2 and QA 12, is still open.
findings.fix: Replace the lid with darkened materials. While !lit(), multiply the storeroom decor and clutter material colours by 0.22 (or swap them to a shared dark toon variant). Keep the cart and cooler as near-black silhouettes with a faint rim, rather than invisible, so the room reads as dark but holding something. Hide the lamp's shade highlight until lit.
findings.verify: Retake v01 and c07. Before lighting, the storeroom is dark, with silhouettes and no plane edge or lamp poking through. After lighting it is the same as now.
findings.verify_reason: In f02 the unlit storeroom shows crates, bins and the floor lamp clearly through a purple tint. The darkness is a single unlit plane at y 1.5 with opacity 0.8 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:64-66), while the capacitor cart and cooler are made invisible (:293). That breaks DR-76.

findings.title: The winch says 'E Switch the lift on' while nothing feeds it
findings.problem:
Once the capacitor cart is docked, and before any cable feeds it, the prompt at the winch reads 'E Switch the lift on' (s2 log 'cap docked'; lunch-play-c14). Pressing it only sets enabled, and nothing visible happens.

The Playground already uses 'Switch on (needs power first)' for the same situation (src/ui/objectives.ts:80). The Lunch switch prompt doesn't check power (src/lunch-runtime.ts:191-193). For the conveyor and oven it reads the same way.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/lunch-play/s2-clean.mjs log 'cap docked … prompt E Switch the lift on'
findings.fix: In promptAt(), when a switch's load has no closed feed (no lead with to === id, or with cap-lead closed but the cap inlet unfed), say 'Switch the lift on (needs a feed first)', and make the inlet ring pulse.
findings.verify: Retake c14: the prompt mentions the missing feed.
findings.verify_reason: At the 'cap docked' step, before any feed, the prompt was 'E Switch the lift on'. promptAt() reads only load.enabled (src/lunch-runtime.ts:191-193).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lunch-play/v3-clean.mjs log row 'cap docked' prompt 'E Switch the lift on'

findings.title: Too few props for a 33×20 m chaos room: 137 against the Meeting's 310
findings.problem:
snapshot().props is 137 for Lunch (clutter max 160, step 2.4, src/levels/lunch.ts:19), against 310 in the Big Meeting at a similar footprint. The corridor, the widest open space and where the crowd and bots are, is mostly bare floorboards (lunch-play-02, c03, c15).

There are few things to knock over, bowl through with a pushed cart or fling. That makes the throwing and slingshot verbs land on nothing, and the room feels emptier than AGENTS 3 asks for.
findings.fix: Raise clutter.max to 260 and lower step to 2.0. Add kitchen-themed recipes ('dishes': stacked trays, cups and pots; 'crates' near the lift; a 'queue' of food trolleys along the corridor north wall at z 0.8, outside lane r 1.3). Keep the existing lanes, which already protect every route.
findings.verify: snapshot().props ≥ 250. Rerun s2-clean.mjs with no new STUCK legs and the same won time ±5 s.
findings.verify_reason: Measured: snapshot().props is 137 for lunch and 310 for meeting. Clutter is max 160 with step 2.4 (src/levels/lunch.ts:18).

findings.title: The marker reads as a flat yellow floor tag, and step items by the south wall end up under the action bar
findings.problem:
The marker is an unlit yellow cone 0.42 m tall, floating at y 2.1 (src/ui/objectives.ts:97-98, 118), with no outline. At the game camera's pitch it projects well above or away from its target, and reads like a yellow floor decal rather than an arrow. In c02 it hangs in mid-corridor while the mop it points at (2,8) is hidden behind the prompt pill and action bar at the bottom edge.

The doorstop (-3,7), the mop (2,8), the bridges (7-11,8) and the crowd all sit along the south wall, which the follow camera pushes under the bottom HUD whenever Pip is near the kitchen.
findings.fix:
(1) Give the marker an ink outline, a two-tone shade and a 1.6 m vertical drop-line to the target's floor ring.
(2) Size it to at least 24 px at zoom 36.
(3) Draw it with depthTest false.
(4) Move the job items 1.5 m north (z 6.5) off the south wall. Or, when the current step's target projects under the HUD's bounding rect, add a screen-edge arrow.
findings.verify: Retake c02: the mop is visible above the action bar, and the marker crop is at least 24 px with a visible outline.
findings.verify_reason: In c02 the marker is a flat-looking yellow cone hanging in mid-corridor, well above and away from the mop, which sits at the bottom edge behind the action bar. The marker is an unlit cone (radius 0.22, height 0.42) at y 2.1 with no outline (src/ui/objectives.ts:68-69,89 in the current file; the finding's line numbers are shifted).

notes.fun:
What works: Lunch is the richest cable floor so far, and its individual beats are good, physical toys.
- The swing door flaps open as Pip walks through and slams shut behind him.
- Mopping shrinks the puddle you're standing in.
- Two cleaner bots patrol a painted loop and drag the mop around (it ended up at (12.35,0.39)).
- Powering the feed post has a clear payoff: the cable lights with pulses, the oven window glows, and the storeroom lights up to reveal the capacitor cart (c07).
- Docking the cart gives a satisfying spark and plug sound.
- The dolly drag feels weighty.
- Throwing the doorstop at the lunch crowd raised two '!' alarm bubbles (x06, DR-04 passes).
- The strain colour runs white → orange → red along the thin cable (x03), so the build-up reads.

What hurts:
- The cable's signature slingshot has no payoff. The room is barely longer than the reels: max strain is 0.99 at the east wall, and release moves 0 props.
- There is no fling target or chaos bonus. All three bonuses are 'don't fail' bonuses.
- Prop density is half the Meeting's.
- The fridge timer ends the job at 2:00 for anyone who explores or messes about. That is the opposite of Good Job's promise.
- The win shot drops Pip.
- The grade is effectively always A.

Timing: the bot's clean solve is 91.8 s of simulated time. The longest leg is the 11.5 s cart push, followed by up to 15 s of locked watching at the end. A person will need roughly 3-6 minutes.
notes.playability:
The clean route works end to end (s2-clean: won at 91.8 s, zero console errors on every run). Breaker trips and shorts are recoverable with a cart reset, and the retry click is fast (0.7 s).

Problems found by playing:
- (P0) The doorstop can be thrown behind the conveyor, which is unreachable and never respawns. Without it the door can't be wedged and the job can't be finished without a restart.
- (P0) Pip gets pinned between the wedged right leaf and the doorstop on the natural return path from the lift room. Movement keys do nothing and only a jump frees him.
- The dolly parks in the doorway and stalls later legs. This happened in three runs.
- E near a cart unplugs a working feed when nothing is tripped. A double-tap on reset kills the fridge feed.
- 'E Grab the doorstop' appears at the wedged door, and one press cuts every cable through it.
- The R keycap on Retry and replay does nothing, while R in play reloads instantly.
- The fridge, pendant lamps and half-walls hide Pip at zoom 9.
- At phone size the survey shows only a third of the room.

Performance: 60 fps at 1440×900 on the host GPU. snapshot().drawCalls is about 1230 for Lunch and about 1150 for Meeting, but since src/game.ts:451 now counts every pass (composer and outlines), the PROGRESS table's ~175 is no longer comparable. Re-baseline the table with tools/perf.mjs rather than treating this as a Lunch regression.
notes.clarity:
The scene itself is quite readable.
- On-device state reads well: the needle gauges on the carts, the oven bake dial, the thermometer on the fridge and the sad-food badge over it (f02), the red bolt badge at a cut or short (n02), and the pulsing reset button.
- The fail cards are icon-only and legible: the spoiled bowl or the oven, the thermometer, and the progress chain.
- The 1440×900 survey shows the whole room.
